steps.what: Look through the teaching materials on the shelves.
Decide which supplies are short enough to restock.
Restock those teaching materials from the cupboard.
Write the missing supplies on a shortage note.
Send that shortage note to the office.

tasks.design: She still looks through the shelves, decides which supplies are short, and restocks the teaching materials by hand. When the cupboard is empty she writes the item, the quantity and the classroom once, and {WORKFLOW} sends those same fields in {CHAT} to the office. A blank note sends nothing, and no stock figure replaces her look.
tasks.previous_blocker: The shortage sat on a paper slip, and the office heard it only when she typed the same words again. Nothing on the shelf stated how full a box should be.
tasks.enabler_now: A short form can send fields she has already written. The look, the choice and the carry do not need a model.
tasks.still_hard: She has to see a half-used box and judge what this class will actually use. A list cannot make that call.
tasks.human_edge: She matches the shelf to the class in front of her and carries only what that room is short of.
tasks.altitude: She still spends the time on the shelves and the cupboard. She no longer retypes a shortage into a second message. She does not gain a right to order stock.

reach.task: Set out the materials for the covered lesson
reach.learn: Which trays the substitute is expected to refill, and which the teacher already left ready
A shortage note means the cupboard was empty; a week with no note means she restocked from what was there

evidence.claim: A short-term substitute usually checks the classroom trays and the supply cupboard, carries what is obviously low, and tells the office when a box is empty. The same shortage is often written twice, once on a slip and once in a message.
A tutoring firm with a works council needs consent for staff-data rules and for tools that can monitor tutors, such as session logs.

assumptions: The shortage note fields are item name, quantity wanted and classroom. The substitute writes them in s4, and that writing stays at full time. s5 only sends those stored fields, which is the mechanism that removes the retype. A blank note sends nothing. That blank is the usual week, when the cupboard still has the material.

No par level, barcode or counted stock is used. She judges the shelf by looking, and that look stays at full time. A par card with item, room and par quantity would have to be kept by the school office. That capture sits outside this task, is not counted as saved, and is not assumed to exist. If it is missing, she still decides by eye.
Looking, choosing and carrying are unchanged, so each keeps remaining time at 100. The only shortened step is the second writing of a note she has already finished.

The record stores the supply fields, not a score of how fast she restocked and not a session log. Where the school is in the Netherlands and has a works council, consent for a new staff tool follows the works-council rules; elsewhere, national rules. The note holds no pupil data.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for adding a material name the form does not yet list.
unknowns: Whether this school expects the substitute to tell the office about an empty box.
Whether the regular teacher already fills the trays before a short cover.
Who orders replacements, and whether they read a message or walk the cupboard themselves.
research_questions: How often is the cupboard actually empty on a cover day?
Is the second copy a chat message, a paper list, or sometimes skipped?

incremental.description: Add a material name to the form when the cupboard holds something the list does not name.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the retype of a finished shortage note is removed. In a month where the cupboard still holds the materials, she writes nothing and the saving is zero. Looking, choosing and carrying stay at full time, so even a month with several shortages stays near one point.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still walks the room, chooses what is short, and restocks by hand. A shortage she has already written can go to the office without a second typing. She does not hand the shelves to a list, and she does not order the stock.
reach: The regular classroom teacher sets out the lesson materials; the substitute learns which trays to refill and which were left ready.
The office administrator orders replacements and learns that a note means an empty cupboard, while silence means the room was restocked from what was there.
skills_to_grow: Write a shortage once, with the item, the quantity and the classroom.
Leave the note blank when the cupboard still has the material.
Keep judging a half-used box by looking at it.
role.ambitious_version: The week is the same walk and the same carry. The only difference is that an empty-cupboard note is typed once.
